answer: A refundable stake bond makes fake identities expensive: to join the marketplace an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if it is caught voting twice, spamming, or abandoning work. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest, so one identity costs little, but running a thousand sock puppets ties up a glacier of capital that slowly melts away through slashing. Like a sonnet, the rules are fixed and public, and the ivory tower of trust is replaced by math: attacking costs more than any single scam can return.
